task: Iteration 4 of the great-dirac-w0ytk7 autonomous loop. Iteration 3's side finding: since iteration 2's deadline-swallow fix (30d8dd9) made build_completion_forest genuinely raise TimeoutError on a cooperative decode-deadline instead of silently swallowing it as a fake grammar dead-end, the propagated exception no longer carries the .decode_stats attribute eval_runner.py's per-chunk timeout handler (~line 1161) expects (`stats = getattr(exc, 'decode_stats', None)`) -- so per-record compiler_ms/compiler_prefill_batches telemetry became silently absent (not zeroed, entirely missing) from the suite JSON for every runtime_timeout record. This session fixes that regression and reruns the byte-identical isolated-record protocol to see what the restored telemetry actually shows.
root_cause: eval_runner.py's _generate_chunk_unbounded has two branches that populate decode_stats on timeout. The generate_with_stats branch (single-record path) already did `except BaseException as exc: setattr(exc, 'decode_stats', stats); raise` at the TwoTowerOpenUI.generate_with_stats call site (twotower.py:13998-14000) -- this is why the existing test_evaluate_persists_stats_when_generation_times_out test passed even pre-fix. The generate_batch_requests branch (the one actually exercised by the exposure12 champion's compiler-tree decode path, since batch_size defaults to >1 whenever generate_batch_requests is callable) had no equivalent attach-on-raise: `with collect_decode_stats() as stats: ... predictions = generate_batch_requests(...)` let any exception (including TimeoutError) propagate straight out of the with-block without ever setting exc.decode_stats, even though `stats` (the live, incrementally-mutated DecodeStats bucket) remained a valid, populated local variable at that point.

fix.change: Wrap the generate_batch_requests call(s) in `try: ... except BaseException as exc: setattr(exc, 'decode_stats', stats); raise` inside the existing `with collect_decode_stats() as stats:` block, mirroring TwoTowerOpenUI.generate_with_stats's own attach-on-raise pattern. Purely additive: on the non-exception path, behavior and return value are unchanged.
fix.scope: Observability only -- no change to decode timing, deadline semantics, outcome classification, or any constrained-decoding invariant. Confirmed against AGENTS.md Non-negotiable architecture invariants before editing: this touches only which fields land in the eval suite JSON after a timeout, not any decoding/scoring/bypass/speculation/CRDT/capability-budget behavior.
fix.regression_test_added: tests/test_harnesses/model_build/test_eval_gates.py::test_evaluate_persists_stats_when_batch_generation_times_out (analogous to the existing generate_with_stats timeout test, but exercises the generate_batch_requests branch with a fake model that mutates get_active_stats() then raises bare TimeoutError with no .decode_stats attribute of its own)

falsifiable_question: Does restoring decode_stats telemetry on a propagated TimeoutError reveal that compiler_ms (build_completion_forest's Node-bridge grammar-validation round trip) or something else (trie_ms's neural prefill-batch scoring, backbone_ms) is the dominant remaining cost for the exposure12 champion's 3 timed-out smoke records?
decision: The telemetry fix is a genuine, low-risk, mechanical observability fix (ACCEPT as a fix) and is not itself a claim about ship readiness. The falsifiable question it unblocks is answered: across all 3 isolated smoke records, compiler_ms accounts for 94.95-97.76% of total_ms, with trie_ms (neural prefill-batch scoring, the cost iteration 3's compiler_prefill_max_states cap targeted) and backbone_ms each under 3% of wall time in every record. This is fully consistent with -- not merely assumed by -- iterations 2 and 3's interpretation sections, but is now measured directly from restored per-record telemetry rather than inferred from latency deltas alone. No decode_outcome changed (all 3 records remain runtime_timeout, as expected: this is an observability fix, not a latency fix).
interpretation: compiler_prefill_batches_sum tracks 1:1 with forwards_count_sum in every record (17/17, 86/86, 31/31) confirming iteration 3's read that this counter is a correlated symptom of decode-loop iteration count, not an independent cost driver -- each per-position build_completion_forest call is followed by exactly one prefill batch. The record with the most compiler-tree positions explored (smoke_button_01, 86 forwards) has the lowest compiler_ms percentage (94.95%) because its trie_ms/backbone_ms (905.98ms/865.19ms, both scaling with forwards_count) eat a slightly larger absolute and relative share -- but even there compiler_ms's raw 28486ms dwarfs everything else. There is no record in this sample where a non-compiler_ms cost is anywhere close to competitive. Any future latency-reduction attempt on this suite must target build_completion_forest's own per-call cost (the Node-bridge grammar-validation round trip identified but not yet root-caused in decode-compiler-tree-lexer-cache-hero-rerun-20260728.md's next-steps) -- bounding prefill batch width (iteration 3) or fixing lexer caching (iteration 1) alone cannot move a 95-98%-dominated wall.
scope_note: No claim about the exposure12 champion's quality or promotion status. No claim that this telemetry fix changes wall-clock latency or decode_outcome for any record (it does not, by design -- it only restores diagnostic fields on an already-correct TimeoutError classification). No re-investigation of build_completion_forest's own internal cost breakdown (still open).
non_goals: No latency improvement claimed or found.
No change to decode_timeout_seconds, deadline semantics, or outcome classification.
No GPU or real-scale training run.
next_steps: Root-cause build_completion_forest's own per-call cost (the Node-bridge grammar-validation round trip) with the now-restored per-record telemetry as a starting instrument -- e.g. does compiler_ms scale linearly with compiler_prefill_tokens_sum (4352/22016/7936 across the 3 records) or is there a large fixed per-call overhead independent of token count?

Consider whether the Node-bridge round trip itself (subprocess spawn + JSON marshal per validate() call, per src/slm_training/dsl/lang_core.py's _invoke_once) is amortizable -- a persistent bridge process instead of one-shot subprocess.run per call would be a genuinely new architectural direction, not yet attempted in this doc chain.
